# Matching exercise

Effect of NSW program on 1978 earnings of male participants.

The dataset has several variables for each participant.

```{r}
summary(lm(re78 ~ treat + black + education + married + hispanic , data = nsw ))
```

based on your interviews with the designers of the experiment, you discover that four strata were created, before being used to randomize treatment. 

The strata were formed based on: 

* being a person of color yes or no (1/0, variable "black"), 
* as well as not having at least 10 years of education (in the 1970s secondary education was mandatory until age of 16) (1/0, variable "hi_edu"). 

This creates four strata in the data.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(lalonde)

dfstrat <- nsw %>%
  mutate(hi_edu= if_else(education >= 10, 1, 0)) %>%
  select(black, hi_edu, treat, re78)
```

# Method 3: nearest neighbour matching

Then later on, from one of the participants you learn that "age"  also played a role in treatment assignment. 
Luckily, you also have data on the age of participants.

We are now assuming that treatment was random given a persons age, that person being a person of color, and whether that person had finished high school.

c) Can you still use the subclassification method? Do all strata have common support?
